# Jeroen Monnee {.hero-name}

:::: {.hero-role}
Postdoctoral Researcher · II. Institute for Theoretical Physics · University of Hamburg
::::

:::: {.hero-lead}
I use **asymptotic Hodge theory and Calabi–Yau geometry** to understand boundary
regimes of string compactifications—where towers of states become light, strings
emerge, and effective theories encounter quantum-consistency constraints.
::::

:::: {.hero-support}
My work connects abstract structures in geometry to concrete questions about
effective field theory, duality, and the microscopic origin of quantum gravity.

Research programme

## Geometry as a diagnostic of quantum gravity
::::

:::: {.section-intro}
The geometry of a compactification is not merely background data: it controls
masses, couplings, field-space distances, and the appearance of new degrees of
freedom. I study this structure in asymptotic regimes where universal statements
become possible.
::::
:::::

::::: {.theme-grid}

:::: {.theme-card}
::: {.theme-number}
01
:::
### Infinite distance and emergence

I identify the towers of light states, effective strings, and higher-dimensional
descriptions associated with boundaries of Calabi–Yau moduli spaces.

[Read about this theme](research.qmd#infinite-distance){.card-link}
::::

:::: {.theme-card}
::: {.theme-number}
02
:::
### Hodge theory as a physical toolkit

I translate structural results on degenerating Hodge structures into practical
control over periods, metrics, couplings, flux potentials, and BPS masses.

[Read about this theme](research.qmd#hodge-theory){.card-link}
::::

:::: {.theme-card}
::: {.theme-number}
03
:::
### Quantum consistency and finiteness

I investigate when classical limits survive quantum corrections and how geometry
constrains the landscape of effective theories and flux vacua.

[Read about this theme](research.qmd#quantum-obstructions){.card-link}
::::

## Recent and representative publications
::::

:::: {.section-intro}
These papers illustrate the main strands of my research: geometric interpretations
of infinite-distance limits, the emergence of strings and Kaluza–Klein towers, and
quantum obstructions to apparently consistent classical limits.
::::
:::::

::::: {.work-grid}

:::: {.work-card}
::: {.work-meta}
Physical Review D · 2026 · Two-paper series
:::
### Quantum obstructions for $\mathcal{N}=1$ infinite-distance limits

Quantum effects can strongly alter—or even remove—classical infinite-distance
regimes, requiring different moduli sectors to scale together.

::: {.work-links}
[Part I: DOI](https://doi.org/10.1103/blb9-hrwd)
[Part I: arXiv](https://arxiv.org/abs/2603.12315)
[Part II: DOI](https://doi.org/10.1103/ypyx-mg6r)
[Part II: arXiv](https://arxiv.org/abs/2603.13470)
:::
::::

:::: {.work-card}
::: {.work-meta}
Journal of High Energy Physics · 2026
:::
### Physics and geometry of complex-structure limits

The Hodge-theoretic classification of type II, III, and IV limits is connected to
explicit vanishing cycles, towers of BPS states, and higher-dimensional duality frames.

::: {.work-links}
[DOI](https://doi.org/10.1007/JHEP03(2026)063)
[arXiv](https://arxiv.org/abs/2509.07056)
:::
::::

:::: {.work-card}
::: {.work-meta}
Journal of High Energy Physics · 2026
:::
### Emergent strings in Type IIB Calabi–Yau compactifications

A microscopic construction identifies emergent heterotic strings and their
accompanying towers of light states in a broad class of type II limits.

::: {.work-links}
[DOI](https://doi.org/10.1007/JHEP01(2026)140)
[arXiv](https://arxiv.org/abs/2504.01066)
:::
